study type: Secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial
exposure: Evidence-based surgical measures (prophylactic antibiotics administered before skin incision, chlorhexidine-alcohol for skin antisepsis, closure of subcutaneous layer if subcutaneous depth is >=2 cm, subcuticular skin closure with suture)
outcome: Composite of wound complications (surgical site infection, cellulitis, seroma, hematoma, separation within 30 days)
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 1082 patients who underwent cesarean delivery and had follow-up data from a randomized controlled trial on skin antisepsis.
finding: The risk of wound complications was significantly lower in patients who received all four evidence-based measures compared with those who did not.
mod_finding: Among patients who received all evidence-based measures, unscheduled cesarean delivery was the only significant residual risk factor for wound complications and surgical site infection.
